meta.title: RAG: how Juno's real posts reach Claude

cards.title: What Voyage is
items: An AI company that makes embedding models. We call its voyage-4 model over HTTP (packages/providers/src/voyage/embed.ts).
An embedding model reads a piece of text and returns a fixed list of 1,024 numbers: a point on a map of meaning.
It never writes or decides anything. It only turns text into numbers so meaning can be compared with maths.

cards.title: How numbers capture meaning
items: The model was trained so texts that mean similar things land at nearby points, even with no words in common.
"what games u into" and a caption like "fortnite all night" share no words but sit close together.
Closeness is measured as cosine distance: the angle between two points. Smaller angle, more related.

cards.title: R: Retrieve (top row once, bottom row every reply)
items: Once: each of her 1,025 chunks is embedded and saved next to its text (examples/app/scripts/persona/load.ts).
Every reply: only the fan's message is embedded. One SQL query ranks every stored chunk by distance to it.
The 5 closest come back as plain text. The other 1,020 never leave the database.

cards.title: A: Augment
items: Those 5 texts are pasted into Claude's prompt under "Things she has said or posted".
Alongside them: the persona card, what we know about this fan, and the recent chat.
Claude never sees a price, and never sees the other 1,020 chunks.

cards.title: G: Generate
items: Claude Haiku writes the reply grounded in her real words: real facts (her cat, her stream) and her phrasing.
Without retrieval it would have to invent details, or sound like generic rules.
The draft then goes to Jev's verify check before the fan sees it.

cards.title: Why 5, why vectors, what if it breaks
items: All 1,025 every time would be huge, slow and noisy. 5 short chunks cost a few hundred tokens.
Measured: the right chunk was in the top 5 for 67% of test questions by vector, 17% by keywords.
If Voyage errors or rate-limits, the bottom path ranks by keywords instead, so a reply still goes out.
